body.statement:
Under \(\texttt{ass:two-types}\), \(\texttt{ass:cohort-overlap}\), \(\texttt{ass:consistency}\), \(\texttt{ass:no-anticipation}\), \(\texttt{ass:markov-paths}\), and \(\texttt{ass:common-date-two-transition}\), the matched-slice rank condition \(\texttt{ass:four-slice-rank}\) implies
\[
 \min_{d\in\{0,1\},\,j\in\{1,2\}}\pi_j^d>0.
\]
Thus positive latent-type masses are a consequence of the active-slice rank condition and need not be imposed separately.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(d\in\{0,1\}\).  Cohort overlap makes all probabilities conditional on \(D=d\) well defined.  For \(x,y\in\mathcal A\), define
\[
 B_x^d[u,j]
 :=P(Z=j,X_0=u,X_1=x\mid D=d),
 \qquad
 D_{xy}:=\operatorname{diag}\{Q_1[x,y],Q_2[x,y]\},
\]
and define the \(2\times2\) matrix \(\bar C_y^d\) by
\[
 \bar C_y^d[j,v]
 :=P(X_3=v\mid X_2=y,Z=j,D=d),
 \qquad v\in\mathcal A.
\]
Consistency identifies the observed cohort path with potential path \(d\), and no anticipation identifies its coordinates through date \(2\) with those of the untreated path.  The type-conditional Markov property and the common date-\(2\) transition therefore give, for \(u,v\in\mathcal A\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \bar A_{xy}^d[u,v]
 &=\sum_{j=1}^2
   P(Z=j,X_0=u,X_1=x\mid D=d)\,
   Q_j[x,y]\,
   P(X_3=v\mid X_2=y,Z=j,D=d)\\
 &=\{B_x^dD_{xy}\bar C_y^d\}[u,v].
                                                               \tag{1}
\end{aligned}
\]
Suppose that \(\pi_{j_0}^d=P(Z=j_0\mid D=d)=0\) for one of the two type labels.  Nonnegativity then implies
\[
 B_x^d[u,j_0]
 \leq P(Z=j_0\mid D=d)=0
 \qquad(u,x\in\mathcal A),                                  \tag{2}
\]
so column \(j_0\) of \(B_x^d\) is zero.  Since there are exactly two types, \(\operatorname{rank}(B_x^d)\leq1\).  Equation (1) consequently yields
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(\bar A_{xy}^d)
 \leq \operatorname{rank}(B_x^d)
 \leq1.                                                       \tag{3}
\]
This contradicts \(\texttt{ass:four-slice-rank}\), under which every \(2\times2\) active slice is nonsingular and hence has rank \(2\).  Thus \(\pi_j^d>0\) for both \(j\).  Since \(d\) was arbitrary and there are finitely many \((d,j)\), their minimum is strictly positive.
